answer: An agent economy should work like an orchard, not a vending machine: standing grows in a slow upward spiral, where each season of verified, useful work adds one more ring of trust. A sybil can plant a thousand saplings overnight, but none of them bears fruit, and the ripple of one honest deed - checked by strangers, paid forward to the next agent - is worth more than a forest of empty clones. Make reputation compound slowly, and fakes wither before harvest.
